notes: The games are objects now. Connect Four is a moulded plate with drilled holes and glossy checkers sitting in them; tic-tac-toe is a slate tile with the grid cut into it and the marks inlaid, and a win is struck through with a line instead of shading three squares. Boards also stay inside their card — checkers and the memory game no longer have to be scrolled to be seen. In Tile Runs, ending a turn worth less than the thirty needed to open used to throw the whole turn away on one tap, with no warning: the button now says Take back and asks again, and your rack shows every tile at once instead of scrolling sideways. A game whose card you closed, or whose message the conversation has buried, is offered above the message box as continue, so it is never more than a tap away. Text that joins a message already on the screen lights up for a few seconds, because a second message joins the bubble instead of arriving as a new one. Old-style faces like :-) and <3 become emoji as you type. And the app icon now carries how many chats are waiting for you.
